scams.name: Friendship Bracelet/String Scam
scams.description: Someone approaches you in a friendly manner and loops a coloured string or bracelet around your wrist before you can refuse. Once it's tied on, they claim it's a 'gift' and then aggressively demand cash payment, typically 5-20 euros. They may physically grab your wrist to tie the bracelet, creating social pressure by making a scene if you try to walk away without paying.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets when walking through tourist areas. Say 'Non, merci' firmly and keep walking. If they grab your wrist, firmly remove their hand and walk away.
scams.location: Old Port (Vieux-Port), La Canebière, tourist areas

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A passer-by 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near you, showing it and claiming it's yours or that you must have dropped it. When you say it's not yours, they offer to let you have it as it 'must be your lucky day.' They then ask for a reward or 'finder's fee.' The ring is worthless brass that cost them almost nothing.
scams.avoidance: Ignore anyone claiming to have found something valuable. Say 'Non, ce n'est pas à moi' (No, it's not mine) and walk away. Never accept items from strangers.
scams.location: Old Port, La Canebière, near train stations, tourist walkways

scams.name: Pickpocketing
scams.description: Marseille has significant pickpocketing issues, especially in tourist areas. Thieves work in groups using distraction techniques: children swarming near the train station, someone asking directions while another lifts your wallet, creating commotions, or standing unusually close on the metro and grabbing items as doors close. Gare Saint-Charles has a particularly heavy concentration.
scams.avoidance: Wear a cross-body bag in front, not behind. Keep phones out of back pockets. Never sling a bag over a chair back at outdoor tables. Use a money belt for large amounts. Be extra vigilant when metro doors open and close.
scams.location: Vieux-Port, Gare Saint-Charles, Metro Line 1, La Canebière, crowded markets

scams.name: Fake Charity Petition Scam
scams.description: A person approaches with a clipboard, often claiming to be deaf-mute, asking if you speak English. They request you sign a 'petition' for a charity. The petition is in English (a red flag in France). After signing, they demand a donation. While distracted, an accomplice may pickpocket you.
scams.avoidance: Never stop for clipboard petitioners. Say 'Non' firmly and keep walking. Never sign anything on the street. Legitimate French charities don't solicit cash on the street.
scams.location: Vieux-Port, tourist attractions, Gare Saint-Charles, La Canebière

scams.name: Three Card Monte / Shell Game
scams.description: You encounter a group around someone playing a card or shell game. People (accomplices) appear to win easily. When you play, you lose every time due to sleight of hand. The game depends on a lookout, a 'roper' to bring players, and shills who pretend to win. Some become aggressive if you try to leave without paying.
scams.avoidance: Never play street gambling games - they are always rigged. Do not stop to watch. Remember bystanders are likely accomplices. The shell game is fraud in France.
scams.location: Busy tourist areas, near Old Port, public squares, near train stations

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging / Unlicensed Taxi
scams.description: Unlicensed drivers or unscrupulous licensed drivers target tourists at the airport or train station. They may refuse to use the meter, quote inflated prices, take long routes, or claim the meter is broken. Some unlicensed operators solicit inside terminals. Official airport-to-city fare is approximately €50 daytime, €60 at night.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxis from designated ranks. Confirm fare before getting in. Insist on the meter. Know approximate fares in advance. Use Uber for transparent pricing. Note driver ID if overcharged.
scams.location: Marseille Provence Airport, Gare Saint-Charles, outside nightlife areas

scams.name: Restaurant Overcharging
scams.description: Tourist restaurants use tactics to overcharge: menus with reasonable prices but higher bills, expensive 'specials' not priced, items added that weren't ordered, automatic bottled water instead of free tap water, insisting tourists must tip (service is included in France), different menus/prices for tourists vs locals.
scams.avoidance: Ask for the French menu and compare prices. Request 'une carafe d'eau' (tap water) - it's free. Verify prices for specials before ordering. Review bill carefully. Tipping is not required in France. Choose restaurants away from main tourist areas.
scams.location: Restaurants around Vieux-Port, heavily touristed areas

scams.name: ATM Skimming / Card Trap
scams.description: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs that capture card data and PIN. This includes overlays on card slots, fake keypads, or hidden cameras. In card trap version, your card gets stuck and a 'helpful' stranger appears, watching you enter your PIN. Once you leave, they retrieve your card.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours. Cover keypad when entering PIN. Check for loose or unusual parts before inserting card. If card gets stuck, don't leave - call your bank. Never accept help from strangers at ATMs.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs in tourist areas, dimly lit locations, non-bank ATMs

scams.name: Fake Police Scam
scams.description: Two people in official-looking clothes flash fake badges quickly, claiming to be 'Tourist Police.' They claim they need to check your wallet for counterfeit bills or verify identity. While examining your wallet, they steal cash. Some variations demand immediate cash 'fines' for supposed violations.
scams.avoidance: Real French police never check tourists' wallets on the street. Ask to see ID clearly and note badge number. Insist on going to nearest police station before handing anything over. Never give your wallet to anyone on the street. Call 17 if suspicious.
scams.location: Streets near tourist areas, public transportation, near bars at night

scams.name: Bump and Spill Distraction Theft
scams.description: A well-dressed person 'accidentally' spills something on your clothing. They apologize profusely and help wipe off the stain while an accomplice steals your wallet or phone. Variations include a jogger bumping you hard or someone dropping coins near you - as you help, an accomplice grabs your bag.
scams.avoidance: Immediately check belongings if anyone spills on or bumps you. Don't let strangers touch your clothing. Step back from anyone getting too close. Keep bags secured in front of you.
scams.location: Metro stations, crowded tourist areas, outside cafes

scams.name: Rental Car Break-in / Smash and Grab
scams.description: Marseille and Provence are notorious for car break-ins targeting tourists, especially at beaches and the Calanques. Thieves identify rental cars by plates, sterile interiors, and stickers. They smash windows and steal bags in seconds. Some target cars in traffic, grabbing items through open windows at red lights.
scams.avoidance: Never leave anything visible in the car - even empty bags look promising. Remove rental car stickers if possible. Park in attended lots. Never park near Calanques trailheads with valuables. Keep windows closed even in traffic. Load trunk before arriving at destination.
scams.location: Calanques parking areas, beach parking lots, roadside stops, scenic viewpoints

scams.name: Vacation Rental / Airbnb Scam
scams.description: Scammers create fake vacation rental listings using stolen photos from legitimate properties. The listing shows an attractive apartment at below-market prices. Victims pay deposits, then arrive to find the property doesn't exist, belongs to someone else, or is drastically different. Some hosts cancel just before check-in offering inferior substitutes.
scams.avoidance: Book only through established platforms with buyer protection. Never pay outside the platform. Read reviews carefully and check host history. Reverse image search listing photos. If price seems too good to be true, it probably is.

scams.name: Beach Theft at Prado Beaches
scams.description: While tourists swim or relax, thieves steal unattended belongings from beach towels and bags. The Prado beaches have shaded areas providing cover for thieves. At the Calanques, visitors leave belongings while swimming, making easy targets. Some thieves work in pairs - one distracts while the other takes items.
scams.avoidance: Never leave valuables unattended on the beach. Use a waterproof pouch for phone and money while swimming. Take turns watching belongings with companions. Leave valuables at accommodation. Use beach lockers where available.
scams.location: Prado beaches, urban beaches, Calanques swimming areas
